title: One Sweetly Solemn Thought
description: One Sweetly Solemn Thought in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Phoebe Cary wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 531.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: One sweet-ly sol-emn thought Comes to me o’er and o’er,— Near-er my home to day am I Than e’er I’ve been be-fore;

lines: Comes to me o’er and o’er,—
Nearer my home to-day am I
Nearer to-day the great white throne;
Nearer to leave the heavy cross;
There rolls the silent, unknown stream
That leads at last to light.
And I to-day am nearer home,
Nor let me stand at last alone

licence: Public domain: Phoebe Cary died in 1871.
credits: Words by Phoebe Cary (1824–1871), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
